items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: Ori used to play a tram on... Uh, uh, uh, with King Oliver.

ctx.x: They had home. I forgot the name. Did you ever hear, uh... Ori and Oliver play together down here? Who?
Ori and Oliver. Oh yeah, sure. Ori used to play a tram on... Uh, uh, uh, with King Oliver.
Uh, right when I checked that right there now on, uh, on, uh, Tremont Street.

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: King Oliver was a man listening, playing music, long listening.

ctx.x: No, no. King Oliver was a man listening, playing music, long listening. Came up and playing music, long. See, I just listened. I taught in tramo in 1970. Them people had been playing. And Poetsy? That's right. People had been playing, man. And I learned fast. Because I stole what I got. I stole that. Everything I learned in tramo, I stole it. I go by you, Dick, how you make that dick? I take that and go and, I'm not spiraling, but I'm going to make it, and I get it together. New York, but I'm going to put more…

You were talking about the number of jobs you had, and how there was a dance, you know, every night, more than one place. And it sounds as though New Orleans was, you know, really living for music in those days. This is the way it sounded to us, say, New York. Every time we said jazz, of course, all we thought of was New Orleans.
